findings.text: Getgroups entry reports the current credential group count and optionally copies the set to user memory. Negative size fails as invalid; a non-zero size smaller than the stored count fails as invalid; copy failure surfaces as a fault. Zero size only queries the count.

Setgroups entry allows a privileged caller to replace the current supplementary set with a sorted imported set bounded by the maximum. Permission failure, oversize, allocation failure and import failure leave current state unchanged and report distinct errors.

Current group replacement uses a prepare, mutate, security check, then commit or abort credential transaction. Allocation failure reports out of memory; security veto aborts without installing; otherwise the new credential becomes current.
Setgroups permission requires setgid capability in the current user namespace together with namespace allowance. Namespace allowance requires an established GID mapping and an explicit allow flag.
Namespace setgroups allowance reads mapping extent state and flags under a dedicated state mutex, giving a consistent snapshot against concurrent mapping or flag updates.
Group count query reads current credential group state without task locking because the referenced state is stable for the reader.

Hung determination classifies a thread as hung only when it remains in uninterruptible sleep without killable, no-load or frozen qualifiers, has switched at least once, shows no recent switch-count progress, and its last switch time exceeds the configured timeout.

A dedicated kernel thread supervises hung tasks periodically. Effective interval is the smaller of timeout and check interval, defaulting interval to timeout when zero. A due deadline triggers a scan unless a reset was requested or the detector is suspended for power management; zero timeout disables scanning with an unbounded sleep.

Each scan that finds hung threads increments a global detection counter and a per-round count, emits a report while warnings remain or panic is armed, consumes warning budget, refreshes configured system info, and panics when the panic threshold is reached. Scans are skipped after a fatal taint or a prior panic notification.

Hung scan holds RCU across thread iteration with a time-based break that pins both process and thread, drops RCU, yields, reacquires RCU and continues only if both remain alive. Maximum visited entries is bounded by a tunable count.

Detect-count control exposes the atomic counter for read and accepts only zero on write to clear it, rejecting non-zero writes. Timeout and interval controls use the unsigned-long vector handler where available and otherwise report unimplemented; after a successful write they wake the supervisor thread.

Hung detector sysctl table publishes tunable entries for backtrace, panic threshold, check count, timeout, interval, warning budget, detect count and info mask, with numeric range handlers and read-write mode. Timeout and interval share a common maximum; backtrace entry exists only on multiprocessor builds.

Hung detector constants and defaults: lock-break interval is one tenth of a tick second; timeout maximum is the largest long scaled by tick rate; default check count is the process ID limit; default timeout and panic defaults come from build configuration; check interval defaults to zero meaning follow timeout; initial warning budget is ten; detect counter starts at zero; info mask starts clear.

Blocked-task diagnosis is RCU-guarded and does nothing without blocker annotation or in minimal builds. Where present it resolves mutex, semaphore and reader or writer semaphore blockers to an owner, reports missing owners, matches owners against live threads to report likely ownership, and dumps the owner unless it is itself hung.

Memory remap maps a physical range with requested cacheability, trying write-back first, then write-through, then write-combining until one succeeds. Empty flags, mixed RAM overlap and non-write-back aliasing of RAM fail without mapping; mixed and alias cases warn.

Write-back requests intersecting RAM first attempt direct-map reuse when the frame is valid, low and permitted by architecture; otherwise they fall back to an architecture mapping that prefers cached mapping when available.

Device-managed remap allocates a tracked slot, maps the range, and on success binds the mapping to the device for automatic release; allocation failure reports out of memory and mapping failure reports absence. Explicit unmanage releases by address match with a warning if absent. Plain unmap only tears down ioremap addresses.
Physical overlap queries hold a resource read lock during tree inspection. Atomic notifier registration serializes chain mutation with interrupt-saving spin locking.

Overlap classification returns disjoint when no extent matches the requested type, intersecting when every overlapping extent matches including descendant coverage that may split a parent window, and mixed when matched and unmatched extents both overlap. Type match requires all requested flag bits plus either wildcard or exact descriptor equality.

Lazy interrupt work uses per-CPU raised and deferred queues plus a per-CPU worker thread. A wake helper awakens the worker only when deferred work is pending and the worker exists; the should-run predicate reports pending deferred work.

Hazards include warnings on mixed RAM remap attempts and on aliasing RAM with incompatible cacheability, suppression of further hung reports after the warning budget expires, and forced panic once the configured hung count threshold is met in a round.

Detector startup registers a panic notifier that records panic entry, installs a power notifier that suspends scanning across suspend, hibernation and restore preparation until completion, starts the supervisor thread, and publishes sysctls where supported. An external reset request causes the next due scan to be skipped once.
